newsitem.title: CYPRUS: U.N. peacekeepers probe Cyprus shooting incident.
newsitem.headline: U.N. peacekeepers probe Cyprus shooting incident.

text.p: United Nations forces in Cyprus launched an inquiry into a shooting incident reported between Greek and Turkish Cypriots on the divided island on Thursday, U.N. officials said.

Opposing sides on the divided island gave different accounts of the incident, which took place between 2.00 and 3.00 a.m. (midnight-0100 GMT) in the vicinity of the Turkish-held village of Louroujina, 20 km (12 miles) southeast of Nicosia.
U.N. spokesman Waldemar Rokosewski said the force had initial information shots were fired by both sides, but later clarified this was according to claims made by the Turkish military.
"There was a claim by the Turkish army shots were delivered by the (Greek Cypriot) National Guard. We have no confirmation of this (now)," he told Reuters, adding that enquiries were continuing.
"An additional deployment of (U.N.) troops in the area led to a lowering of tension and things returned to normal," he added.

U.N. troops stationed on Cyprus man a buffer zone which has separated the two communities since Turkey invaded Cyprus's north in 1974 after a Greek Cypriot coup in Nicosia engineered by the military then in power in Greece.
The Turkish Cypriots established their own state in northern Cyprus in 1983, which is recognised only by Ankara.
"At 0300 hours our patrol guards spotted two armed men attempting to lower our flag and three other armed men were spotted taking up position," Turkish Cypriot official Taner Etkin said.

"They opened fire to give cover to the two intruders and our patrol guards returned the fire. They escaped but blood stains were traced going across the buffer zone to the south," he said. "We have lodged a very strong protest with the U.N."
Rokosewski refused to say whether blood was found in the area.

Yiannakis Cassoulides, spokesman for the Greek Cypriot-led Cyprus government, categorically denied claims the army was involved in any incident and said police had no information of civilian injuries or suspicious movements in the area.

"Our National Guard denies any involvement whatsoever in the alleged incident," he told Reuters. "There have been no casualties in the National Guard and all the National Guard arms have been checked and they have not been used."
"The only thing we confirm is that around 2 a.m. our National Guard heard shots within the (Turkish) occupation lines," he added.
Cyprus police spokesman Glafcos Xenos said the U.N. informed them Turkish forces "fired against two persons allegedly approaching their positions from the free areas".
"According to what we have been told (by the UN) they were holding rifles and ran off towards the direction of the free areas when Turkish forces fired shots in their direction," he said.

Tensions in Cyprus were fanned last month by a row over Greek Cypriot plans to deploy anti-aircraft missiles in the south of the island and Turkish threats of a military strike to block their deployment.
Four Greek Cypriots and one Turkish Cypriot soldier were killed in violent incidents last year in and around the island's buffer zone.

U.N. efforts spanning decades to reunite the island under a bi-zonal federation have floundered, while the dispute remains a source of tension between Greece and Turkey, NATO allies but bitter rivals in a volatile region.
